reading.body:
Flexential Portland - Hillsboro 3 publishes 36 MW of IT capacity across 358,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 36 MW supports roughly 900 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a more typical colocation average, the same power supports roughly 3,600 racks. The arithmetic is an illustration of range, not an operator claim. The floor area works out to about 10 watts per square foot at the higher density figure, which is consistent with a facility built for mixed workloads rather than one optimized purely for dense GPU clusters.

The certification stack qualifies this campus for a specific set of regulated and sensitive workloads. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 address financial and operational controls. PCI DSS covers payment card data. HITRUST and NIST 800-53 address healthcare and federal security frameworks respectively. ITAR restricts access to controlled defense-related technical data, which limits who can physically and logically enter the relevant portions of the facility. SSAE 18 is the auditing standard under which the SOC reports are issued, not a separate substantive control. Which tenants occupy the campus is not published.

Among Oregon facilities this site has read, Hillsboro 3 ranks first by published IT megawatts, accounting for 36 of the 182 MW recorded across the six facilities in the state that have published a figure at all. Oregon has 133 facilities mapped in OpenStreetMap, and most publish no capacity number, so the 182 MW total is a floor on state capacity, not a ceiling. The campus sits in Hillsboro, which is part of the Portland metro area and has attracted significant data center investment because of available land, fiber density, and proximity to Pacific routes. None of those secondary factors are in the operator's published specifications, so their weight here is observational context only.
